original_question: If X is a weakly compactly generated Banach space, must X admit a norming Markushevich basis; that is, a biorthogonal system whose coefficient functionals span a norming subspace of X*?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the John-Zizler question: the paper's classical WCG-versus-norming-Markushevich-basis problem, stated historically in the Introduction and formulated explicitly again as Problem 4.1 in Section 4.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right Banach-space class (weakly compactly generated spaces) and the right property (existence of a norming Markushevich basis). It also correctly points to the dual-side norming requirement, which is the central feature of a norming M-basis in the paper.
missing_details: A norming Markushevich basis is not just any biorthogonal system: it must be a Markushevich basis, so the primal vectors must be fundamental, i.e. the linear span of the vectors is dense in X.
In the non-separable setting, the object is generally an indexed family {(x_i, x_i^*)}_{i in I}, not necessarily a sequence; the official problem is not restricted to countable systems.

The norming condition should be stated precisely: span{x_i^* : i in I} must be a norming subspace of X^*, equivalently there exists lambda >= 1 such that sup{|f(x)| : f in B_{span{x_i^*}}} >= lambda^(-1) ||x|| for every x in X.

Because a norming subspace is automatically weak*-dense, totality on the dual side is implicit once norming is imposed; the missing structural condition in your draft is chiefly density of the primal vectors.
The nearby official sharpening in the paper is that one may reduce the problem to WCG spaces of the form C(K); your draft does not mention this equivalent reformulation.
The nearby characterization of shrinking M-bases involves extra Asplund/shrinking hypotheses; those are contextual but are not part of the John-Zizler question itself and should not be added.
refined_question: Does every weakly compactly generated Banach space X admit a norming Markushevich basis; that is, does there exist an indexed biorthogonal family {(x_i, x_i^*)}_{i in I} subseteq X x X^* such that overline{span}{x_i : i in I} = X and span{x_i^* : i in I} is a norming subspace of X^* (equivalently, for some lambda >= 1, sup{|f(x)| : f in B_{span{x_i^*}}} >= lambda^(-1) ||x|| for all x in X)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as the paper notes, it is enough to ask this only for weakly compactly generated spaces of the form C(K): does every WCG C(K)-space admit a norming Markushevich basis?
justification: The exact target is the John-Zizler problem. In Section 4, Problem 4.1 asks exactly whether every WCG Banach space admits a norming M-basis. The Introduction presents this as the classical conjectural connection between WCG spaces and norming M-bases. Definition 2.1 gives the precise meaning of a norming M-basis, so the refined version must explicitly require both biorthogonality and density of the primal span. Remark 4.2 gives the paper's official reduction to C(K)-spaces, which is the only alternate formulation that should be retained. Theorem 4.3 supplies nearby context by showing that the stronger shrinking-M-basis problem belongs to the WCG-plus-Asplund setting, so the refined question should not import those extra hypotheses.
